sections.title: Mit, mennyit, hány kilót
sections.content: At the market the seller asks what and how much you want. You know *mit?* (what, as an object). *Mennyi* (how much) works the same way: as an object it takes *-t*, so *Mennyit kérsz?* means "How much do you want?". To ask for a number of kilos, use *hány*; the noun stays singular and takes *-t*: *Hány kilót kérsz?* You can answer with only the amount: *Egy kilót kérek.*

sections.title: The seller's questions

sections.content: *Mit*, *mennyit* and *hány kilót* are all objects, but they are not a particular thing, so the verb stays in the form you know: *kérsz*, *kérek*. The definite *kéred* comes only with *a / az* + noun or *ezt / azt*.
